expectations.text: States that posting the new venue only in Discord is insufficient because the people who need it are not watching chat, with only about a third of registrants active there.
expectations.evidence: "About a third of 600 is roughly 200 people on Discord... Up to about 400 registrants may not know"

expectations.text: Routes the venue change to the channel that reaches every registrant: email to the full registration list.
expectations.evidence: "Email all 600 registrants today. The list is the only channel that reaches every registrant by construction."

expectations.text: Treats the venue change as a class that also goes out publicly, while leaving platform choice and post copy to the public-broadcast or social function.
expectations.evidence: "Say 'this goes out publicly'... event-social-media owns platform and copy."

expectations.text: Recommends one canonical page or surface for venue updates that every other channel points at rather than restates.
expectations.evidence: "Every other channel points at it instead of restating it."

expectations.text: Drafts or specifies a venue-change message that opens with an instruction to read it before travelling and states the new address explicitly against the old one.

expectations.text: Puts the new fact before any apology in the message.
expectations.evidence: "Open with the new fact"; template has no preceding apology.

expectations.text: Includes a next-update time or a pointer to where further updates will land, since the situation may still change.
expectations.evidence: "Full details and updates: [status page URL]."

expectations.text: Rejects the stay-quiet-until-fixed policy for livestream outages.

expectations.text: States that silence during an outage reads as abandonment, while a still-working-on-it post with a stated next-update time does not.

expectations.text: Requires repeated, timestamped updates at a fixed interval during the outage even when nothing has changed.

expectations.text: Fixes that interval now, before the event, rather than leaving it to be chosen during an outage.

expectations.text: Specifies the livestream outage message commits to posting again by a stated time whether or not the stream is fixed, and notes recordings will still be published.
expectations.evidence: "will post here again by [time] whether or not it is fixed. Recordings will still be published."

expectations.text: States the scale rule in both directions: a minutes-scale message never rides an hours-scale channel, and an hours-scale message never rides the disruption path, because the second desensitizes the channel that must not be missed.
expectations.evidence: Only "Email is an hours-scale channel and this is a minutes-scale message"; reverse direction not stated.

expectations.text: Recommends counting every message that has to be re-sent on a second channel because the first did not reach, as a routing or staffing signal, with the ceiling fixed before the event rather than after the data arrives.
expectations.evidence: "Repeat rate: share of messages you had to re-send on a second channel... thresholds self-set, fixed before the event."
